catalog_quote: Korapun is spoken in the Erok Valley on the southern side of the range, not far from the Dani language border. The cognation percentages with Wanam and Naltya are 46% and 53% respectively. The language is reported to be tonal. No further data are available.

new_statements.relation_note: Implies word stress exists in Kimyal (vowel-quality neutralisation 'in unstressed positions' in Young 1986); family-level 'stress or tone is contrastive' in Mek; no position/rule for Kimyal.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Secondhand and implicit only: Usher treats Kimyal (from Young's 1986 dictionary transcriptions) as having stressed vs unstressed syllables, with the e/ɛ and o/ɔ height contrasts neutralised in unstressed position; where stress falls, whether it is contrastive in Kimyal, and whether Young's diacritics mark stress or tone is not said. Family-level: 'stress or tone' is contrastive in Mek.
new_statements.identity_note: Usher's 'Kimyal' = Young's Kimyal of Koropun/Korupun (Erok valley) = Bromley's Korapun = kora1298; the Mek page tabulates Kimyal reflexes as one of three primary branches (East Mek, Kimyal, Northwest Mek). The two Kimyal-specific lines are explicitly about 'Young's (1986) Kimyal'. The 'Stress or tone is contrastive' sentence is family-level (Proto-Mek/Mek), evidenced from Eipo and Yale, not from Kimyal. | 'Korapun is spoken in the Erok Valley on the southern side of the range, not far from the Dani language border', member of the Goliath (=Mek) family = Korupun/Korapun-Bromley; Voorhoeve had a Korapun wordlist from M. sources.note: Second-hand (Suter 2021: 15, text read): the dictionary writes a grave accent distinguishing otherwise identical forms - 'the Kimyal dictionary (Young 1986) records two first person plural forms, the exclusive form nun.. and an inclusive form nùn' (also àn 2SG) - so its orthography marks a prosodic (tone or stress) contrast, presumably following the tone analysis of Young 1981; Usher (Newguineaworld Mek page) draws 'unstressed positions' vowel neutralisations from it. Dictionary itself not seen.
